Source: Ainsworth et al., PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases, 2026
texto_aprovado: Its title, though, was won indoors. In 1979, researchers tested the venoms of dangerous snakes on lab mice. They measured the dose that kills half the mice in a test, what scientists call the LD50. The smaller the dose, the more potent the venom, and the inland taipan's came out on top.
